about: THE TOWNS OF THE RHINE DELTA, ZEELAND AND FRISIA, 793-1066 (the ten ports the places files call rhine_frisia): people, bread, what helps and what opens. Written 7 Oct 2026 by a content writer, from Design/content/dossiers and SCHEMAS.md section 1. Every head-count is an estimate: the source of each row says whose it is, and (?) marks our own guess. A draft for the user to overwrite.
how_the_figures_were_made: Nobody counted these places. Where a scholar has given a figure it is used and named: Dorestad 'a few thousand' (Van der Tuuk 2005) and 2,000 to 3,000 (the project's dossier, after Van Es and Verwers); Medemblik 'about twenty houses and 120 to 200 people' (Van Leeuwen 2014); Nijmegen 450 to 650 in the 5th and 6th centuries, from its graves (nl.wikipedia, Geschiedenis van Nijmegen).

Where there is only a dug plan, the figure is houses x 6 people: a house row's length divided by the pitch of its plots (Medemblik: plots proven over 100 m, reckoned at 300 to 450 m; Walichrum: a strip of 1,300 m with houses 5-10 by 14 m; Dorestad: 18 m parcels on the harbour and 'hundreds of houses' over 3 km). That is our reckoning, not a scholar's, and is marked (?).

Graves check the order of size only. Dorestad has at least 2,350 known burials from about 150 years (Van Es and Verwers 1985): at 30 years to a life that is some 470 people living at one time from the dug graveyards alone, and most of the graveyards are not dug. Walichrum has about 116 seen graves from four fields that the sea had mostly taken.
Where nothing is dug (Witla) or the place is one farmstead among several mounds (Wijnaldum), the low and high figures are set wide apart and the best figure is a judgement.

Later rows (after about 900) rest on what was built: a wall 1.9 km long at Deventer, 420 m of revetments at Utrecht, a mint, a chapter of twenty canons. No scholar's figure for these towns before 1066 was found: all are our guesses (?).

endings.text: This year William was bishop at Traiectum and count in West Frisia. The town had its mint, its toll, five great churches and a merchants' quarter on the Vecht side, and the emperor kept Easter there when he chose.

endings.text: In these years Daventre on the IJssel was a greater port than Tiel. Its wall had been closed before the Northmen came, and the sons of the men of Dorestat sat on its bank and struck more pennies than any town between the Rhine and the Elbe.
endings.picture: A long timbered river front crowded with barges under a high earth wall with a palisade; a stone basilica rising behind; carts crossing a ford.

endings.text: The port that was burned in the year of the great fleet did not come back to what it had been. Saint Lebuin's church stood on its dune with fishers' houses round it, and the Saxon road was grass.
endings.picture: A church on a river dune with a dozen thatched houses; eel weirs in a brook mouth; an overgrown earth bank.

endings.text: This year Daventre was the bishop of Traiectum's town, by King Henry's gift of twenty years before, with its toll, its mint and its court. Bernold's church stood over Saint Lebuin, and pennies of Daventre were weighed in the markets of the Northmen and the Rus.
endings.picture: A stone basilica with a westwork above an earth wall and a busy river bank; barges unloading casks; a moneyer's bench under an awning.

endings.text: The king's house at Noviomagus lay burned, but the town under the hill did not need it. It had its own bell, its own barge-wrights and a market that the men of Tiel came up the Waal to.

endings.text: Nobody kept the king's house after the fire. A ferryman and some fishers lived under the old wall, and travellers asked them whose great hall that had been.

endings.text: The palace at Noviomagus, which Charles built and the Northmen burned and the Ottos mended, was burned again in Duke Godfrey's rising and lay so in this year. The bank below it lived by the ferry and the river, and waited for an emperor.
endings.picture: A fire-blackened stone palace and a small standing chapel on a hill above the Waal; a quiet landing below with two barges.

A town work kind 'granary' in story/works_793.json (a common store of grain): the table has the house's storehouse only, so no port here could be given the granary help of living_world.md 1.

Town work kinds for a raised mound and a sea dike in story/works_793.json ('terp' there is a house work): wijnaldum.work.sod_layer, emuthon.work.sods and doccinga.work.dike give a town gift (carry_store) here but have no kind for 'work <port> <kind>', so those rows set no unlock_work flag.

For carry and find_out jobs the 'premium' in a town's asks is meant as a share over the job's pay_d.

A hinge for Traiectum in 1006/1007 (SCHEMAS.md names it utrecht_1006) and place hinges for Witla 836, Walichrum 837 and Daventre 882: each 'fails' row marked turns: true has a help row here, but only Dorestad has a hinge. The endings here test heads and helped only, so they work without those hinges.

The line of Dorestad has a row at 862 (best 900) so that the hinge's test 'st_dorestad_heads >= 1200' can be reached with a mark of about +0.35; on the worked example's line (1,200 in 850 falling straight to 400 in 864) it could not be reached at all.

ports_793.json: Wijnaldum's kind 'royal seat', its end year 850 and Walichrum's end year 850 do not fit the evidence (dossiers, section 8): both places are lived on, as farms, long after. The lines here go on past 850 and the endings are told at 850 because the table says so.
